subject: Model slate, context plan & token cadence — onboarding sync
messages:
From: Ari Morales <ari@novafin.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Quick: model shortlist + context needs for Nov pilot

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We pulled together rough usage expectations for the pilot and want help narrowing the model slate so our engs can wire the retrieval pieces. High-level numbers:
- Pilot DAU: ~1,000 (week 1) ramping to 6,000 over 8 weeks
- Average session: 3 prompts (user prompt + system context + retrieval) + 1 assistant response
- Typical token mix: 650 tokens prompted per session, 1,800 tokens generated on average when retrieval is heavy (summaries + citations)
- Peak single-request context need: ~25k tokens for long-document Q&A; most requests under 4k

As we move from discovery -> pilot, we need a recommended shortlist (2–3 models) with guidance: latency expectations for US region, cost posture, and whether Redwood platform features (prefix caching / KV cache / batching) materially change the recommendation. Also need a monthly token estimate for the pilot and a scoped ask for a dedicated trial if we decide to test 32k context variants.

Attached is our internal sample traffic snapshot. Can you loop in whoever will own the rollout so we can schedule a brief tech handoff?

Cheers,
Ari
Ari Morales
Head of Product, NovaFin
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Ari Morales <ari@novafin.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick: model shortlist + context needs for Nov pilot

Ari — thanks, got the snapshot and good notes. Looping in Monica (CS lead) for token/cost estimates, Grace for latency/ops constraints, and Ben for batching/cache knobs. Quick read from our side and an initial slate below; attaching a two-page shortlist note and the token estimate workbook.

Recommended shortlist (trial phase):
1) Mid-tier quantized (13B, 32k context variant) — recommended default for retrieval-heavy flows where accuracy with documents is important. Expect higher per-token cost but far fewer retrieval fallbacks; good tradeoff for the pilot when accuracy matters.
2) Low-latency 7B quantized (8k context) — best for fast conversational UI and lightweight summarization where latency matters and you can truncate long docs to retrieval snippets. Lower cost per-token and lower memory pressure.
3) Small baseline (3–6B, 8k context) — cheap for non-critical surfaces and bulk tasks (classification, reranking) where throughput matters more than long-context coherence.

Operational guidance:
- For requests under ~4k tokens, prefer 7B; for >6k or heavy retrieval, prefer 13B 32k variant.
- Use prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and recent context (TTL ~10m) to reduce token cost on identical prefixes.
- Precompute embeddings for chunked docs and serve retrieval from a vector DB; only send top-K snippets (truncate to 2–3k) into prompt where possible.
- Batch writes from the ingestion pipeline to the runtime (batch window 20–40ms) — helps throughput without significantly impacting P95 latency for interactive flows.

Open questions for NovaFin:
- Expected simultaneous QPS at pilot start (helps size dedicated pool)
- Tolerance for slightly higher 95th percentile latency during heavy retrieval windows

Next steps: Monica to share token/day and cost estimates; propose a 30-min handoff call tomorrow to align the canary plan and test dataset.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: model_shortlist_notes.pdf (2 pages), novafin_token_estimates.xlsx
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Ari Morales <ari@novafin.com>, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick: model shortlist + context needs for Nov pilot

Ari — thanks for the snapshot. I ran numbers for the pilot and a modest ramp; below are conservative estimates and recommended operational defaults. See attached workbook (tabs: pilot_calc, ramp_calc, assumptions).

Assumptions used (pilot):
- Pilot DAU: 1,000; avg sessions/day per DAU: 1.8
- Avg prompted tokens/session: 650; avg generated tokens/session: 1,200 (we reduced your 1,800 to be conservative for cost planning)
- 12% of sessions will trigger a long-context flow (need >8k context); 2% will need >20k

Estimated monthly tokens (pilot, 30 days):
- Prompt tokens: 1,000 DAU * 1.8 sessions * 650 tokens * 30 = 35,100,000 tokens
- Generated tokens: 1,000 * 1.8 * 1,200 * 30 = 64,800,000 tokens
- Total: ~99.9M tokens/month (round to 100M)

Cost posture (ballpark):
- If majority runs on 7B (8k): lower $/M token — good for chat features.
- If 25–35% of volume uses 13B 32k variant (retrieval), expect a 30–50% uplift in monthly spend vs all-7B.

Operational recommendations (concrete):
- Default routing: small->7B->13B by context/intent rules. Implement rule-based routing in the request layer: if top-K retrieval combined length >3k then prefer 13B.
- Caching: enable prefix caching for system messages and KV cache for recent user turns (keep small per-user KV, evict LRU at 1,000 keys). This should shave 8–12% off prompt token volume in steady state.
- Canary: run pilot on hosted with autoscale but reserve a small dedicated pool for the 32k experiments (single 32k card pool) to avoid throttling while the pilot is small.
- Throughput sizing: for pilot 1k DAU, provision for 20–30 RPS peak; if ramp hits 6k DAU, expect 120–180 RPS.

Action items:
- Ari: confirm whether NovaFin will precompute embeddings for the corpus (recommended) or expect Redwood to host retrieval nodes.
- Grace/Ben: we can provide sample latency profiles for 7B vs 13B in us-west this afternoon.

I can join the handoff call and walk our engineers through the assumptions in the workbook.

—Monica
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Ari Morales <ari@novafin.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple quick clarifications:
1) NovaFin will precompute embeddings for the pilot and host them in our managed vector DB (we'll share access).
2) On 32k: we likely won't need 128k for the pilot, but longer-term we may validate a 100k+ document processing flow. For now, can we scope 32k for pilot and note what it would take to test higher context variants?

I'm available for a 30-min handoff at 2pm PST today if that works for your team. If we sign off on the shortlist, we want Redwood to provision the small dedicated pool for the canary and share a short test plan and expected P95 numbers for both 7B and 13B.

See you at 2 — I'll add the meeting to the shared link and include a short test dataset export.

Best,
Ari
